transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what really made me come in is that I’ve started losing my place a lot at work. I'm a receptionist, and lately, while I’m scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays, my mind just... slips off track. It's like I’m suddenly so busy thinking about what I might have overlooked or forgot to do. 

Which is frustrating because I usually love doing the lobby displays. Just last week I put up this gorgeous autumn arrangement with these little faux pumpkins and maple leaves. I actually found the pumpkins on sale at Michaels, which was a total steal because you know how expensive seasonal decor has gotten lately. I was telling my sister about it—she lives out in Ohio now, and she said her local craft store completely closed down, which is just a shame. She has to drive forty minutes just to get yarn now. 

But, um, anyway, yeah. I'll be in the middle of typing in a client's name for a Tuesday slot and suddenly I'm just staring at the screen, completely lost because my brain is busy worrying about whether I messed up something else.
Do you ever experience sudden episodes of intense anxiety or panic, where your heart races, you feel short of breath, or you worry something bad is going to happen?

No, I don't think I've ever had anything sudden like that. I don't get short of breath or feel like my heart is pounding out of nowhere. 

Well, actually, my heart did race really fast a couple of weeks ago, but I'm pretty sure that was just because I tried that new nitro cold brew at the coffee shop across the street from my office. They just opened up this cute little independent cafe—they took over the space where the old dry cleaners used to be—and they use these special imported beans. The barista was telling me all about their roasting process, which is actually really fascinating. My husband says I spend way too much time talking to the baristas, but honestly, people just like to chat! 

He actually ended up buying me one of those fancy espresso machines for my birthday to try and keep me from buying coffee out so much. You know, the ones with the little milk frother attached? It is absolutely huge, though. I had to completely reorganize my kitchen counters and put my air fryer in the pantry just to make it fit, which is a huge hassle because I use the air fryer for literally everything. I make these little sweet potato fries in there that are just... 

Um, wait, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, the sudden panic things. No, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there isn’t a specific reason for it?

Yeah, I'd say it's most days. It’s just... ordinary things, really. I find myself worrying about the work schedules, or paying the bills, or making little paperwork errors at the front desk. It feels like if I make one small mix-up, it’s going to somehow turn into a much bigger problem. 

Even travel plans have been stressing me out! We're supposed to go visit my sister in Ohio for Thanksgiving, and I’ve been so worried about the rental car. Which, actually, my neighbor Susan rented a car last month when she went down to Florida, and the company completely lost her reservation! She was stuck at the Orlando airport for four hours with her three kids. Can you imagine? Her youngest, Toby, he's a sweet boy but he literally does not stop running. She said she had to buy them all those giant, overpriced airport pretzels just to keep them sitting in their seats. You know the ones, with that awful plastic-looking cheese? I don't know how anyone eats that cheese. It doesn't even need to be refrigerated, which just feels completely unnatural to me. I always tell my husband to check the expiration dates on things like that because you just never know. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the worrying. Yeah, it's just constant little things like that, pretty much every day, where my brain tells me a tiny mistake is going to ruin everything.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work stress?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or hopeless. I still really enjoy the things I normally do, like doing those lobby displays I mentioned. And my gardening! I love my garden. 

Actually, I just planted these beautiful new hydrangeas last weekend. The nursery down the street was having an end-of-season sale, and they had these incredible blue ones. Did you know you can change the color of hydrangeas just by changing the acidity of the soil? It's true! My neighbor Susan—the one who went to Florida—she told me about it. She uses coffee grounds in her soil to make them more blue. Which reminds me, I still have to figure out what to do with all the coffee grounds from that giant espresso machine my husband bought me. It feels like such a waste to just throw them away, you know? I read online that you can make a really good exfoliating body scrub with them if you mix them with coconut oil and a little brown sugar. I bought the coconut oil, but it's been sitting in my pantry for two weeks because I keep forgetting to actually make it. 

Wait, I'm sorry, I did it again, didn't I? What were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling sad. No, I haven't really been feeling sad or anything like that. Just worried.
Do you notice any physical symptoms like restlessness, feeling on edge, muscle tension, or fatigue that seem to go along with your worrying?

Yeah, I do feel really tense a lot of the time. Especially at work. Like, at the front desk I can still smile and help people, but inside I feel so wound tight, you know? Like my shoulders are practically up around my ears and I'm just waiting for something to go wrong. 

Actually, my shoulders have been so bad lately that I finally booked a massage last week. I went to this new place that opened up next to the grocery store—the one with the really good organic produce section. They have these amazing heated massage tables, which felt so nice because it's been getting so chilly in the mornings. I had to dig out my winter coats from the attic, and I realized my favorite wool coat has a tiny hole in the pocket. I don't even know how it got there! I've had that coat for five years, I bought it on clearance at Macy's. They were having one of those huge one-day sales, and I remember because I ran into my cousin Sarah there, and she was buying...

Oh, gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I get so sidetracked. Um, what did you ask? Oh, right, the physical stuff. Yeah, just really tense, especially my shoulders, and feeling like I'm always on edge.
How long have you been feeling this way — the constant worrying and being on edge — and has it been affecting your ability to function at work or home?

Well, it's been a while now. I'd say about nine months? It all started back when there was this whole situation... I had this overnight detention thing, and there was a massive mix-up with the paperwork around it. It was so incredibly stressful. 

Speaking of paperwork, they just changed the whole filing system at the office last month. We used to color-code everything by department—blue for billing, green for human resources, you know. But now they want everything alphabetical, regardless of the department, and they bought these new manila folders that are just terrible quality. The tabs keep bending! I tried to tell the office manager, Brenda, that we should order from the old supplier, but she said they found a cheaper vendor online. Honestly, I don't trust buying office supplies online. My husband bought a stapler off the internet once, and it jammed on the very first day. We had to take the whole thing apart with a screwdriver just to get the staple out, and it scratched the finish on our dining room table. We had just polished that table, too, because we were having his parents over for dinner. His mother is so particular about things being clean, she actually runs her finger over the baseboards when she thinks I'm not looking. 

Wait, I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought again. The worrying, right. Yeah, it's been about nine months since that paperwork mess, and it definitely makes it harder to focus at work sometimes, just constantly feeling like I'm going to mess something up again.
Have you been experiencing this constant worrying and feeling on edge for more than six months?

Yeah, definitely more than six months. Like I was saying, it's been about nine months now, ever since that whole overnight detention thing and the huge paperwork mix-up. 

That paperwork... I still can't believe how badly they bungled it. It reminds me of when my sister tried to do her own taxes last year using that free software online. She thought she was being so smart, saving money on an accountant, but she ended up putting her income on the wrong line and got audited! Can you imagine? Getting audited by the IRS sounds like an absolute nightmare. She had to spend weeks gathering all her receipts, and she keeps them all in this giant shoebox in her closet. I keep telling her she needs to get one of those accordion folders. I have a really nice blue one that I use for all our home warranties and instruction manuals. It's so much easier when everything is organized. I actually bought a label maker just for it—one of those ones where you can change the font? I spent a whole Sunday labeling everything in the house. My husband thought I was crazy, but now he always knows exactly where the spare batteries are... 

Oh, gosh, there I go again. I'm sorry. But yes, to answer your question, it's been going on for about nine months.
